title: Installing and updating
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.

title: Choose your download
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Open the Downloads page . Choose your operating system and processor. Use arm64 for Apple Silicon and most recent Android phones; x64 is for Intel or AMD desktop processors. If you are unsure on Android, choose the universal APK. Use a regular release for everyday use. Development and nightly builds may contain unfinished changes. The Downloads page lists current requirements and package-manager commands. OpenTubeX supports Windows, macOS, Linux, and an Android app . There is no iOS build listed.

title: Windows
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Download the Windows installer matching your processor, or follow the winget instructions . Open the installer and complete its prompts. Launch OpenTubeX from the Start menu. For a portable download, extract the archive before launching the application. Keep the extracted files together.

title: macOS
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Download the DMG for Apple Silicon (arm64) or Intel (x64) . Open it and drag OpenTubeX into Applications . Open OpenTubeX from Applications. OpenTubeX is not notarized by Apple. If the first launch is blocked, allow the app in System Settings → Privacy & Security after checking that you downloaded it from the official release. Homebrew users can follow the Homebrew instructions .

title: Linux
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Choose a package matching your distribution on the Downloads page . Follow the linked repository instructions, or open a downloaded DEB/RPM with your distribution’s package installer. Launch OpenTubeX from your application menu. For an AppImage, open the file’s properties, allow it to run as a program, then launch it. For a portable archive, extract it first and run the included OpenTubeX executable. Repository installations are convenient when you want updates through your normal package manager.

title: Android
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: On the Downloads page , choose F-Droid or Obtainium . For a manual installation, download an APK from GitHub Releases . Follow the selected installer’s prompts. For a direct APK, Android may ask you to allow installation from the browser or file manager you used. Open the app. Allow notifications if you want download progress and playback controls in Android’s notification area. The Android app has a phone layout, background playback, and offline downloads. Desktop integrations, window controls, and external software settings can differ or be unavailable.

title: Update without starting over
description: Choose a release for your device and keep it up to date.
text: Export your data before changing release channels or reinstalling. If you installed through a package manager, F-Droid, or Obtainium, use that same tool to update. For a manual installation, get the newer package for the same platform and install it over the existing app. For a portable installation, keep your existing data when replacing the app files. Reopen the app and check your subscriptions and playlists. On desktop, Settings → General → Check for Updates controls update checks; it does not replace your package manager’s update process. See the Changelog for release changes. Avoid uninstalling or clearing application data just to update.

title: Subscriptions and playlists
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.

title: Find a video or channel
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Enter a title, channel name, or YouTube link in the search field. Submit the search and open a result. Open the channel name to browse more uploads from that creator. OpenTubeX keeps your subscriptions and local playlists in the app. You do not need to sign in to YouTube, and these changes do not update your YouTube account.

title: Subscribe to a channel
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Open the channel you want to follow. Select Subscribe . Open Subscriptions in the navigation to see uploads from your channels. On a small screen, some navigation entries are under More . Use the feed’s refresh action to fetch new uploads. Already have subscriptions elsewhere? Import your existing subscriptions instead of adding channels one by one.

title: Use profiles
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Profiles let you group channels, for example into work and leisure viewing. Open the profile menu from your profile icon. Use the profile selector to choose or manage a profile. Check which profile is active when viewing your subscriptions. If a channel appears to be missing, check All Channels before importing it again. Feed filters can also hide videos, Shorts, or live content. For step-by-step profile creation and bulk channel management, see Organize channels with profiles .

title: Create a local playlist
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Open Playlists in the navigation. Select Create New Playlist . Enter a name and select Create . On a video, use Add to Playlist and choose the playlist. On desktop, video cards also expose actions on hover; use the video’s menu when an action is not visible. Return to Playlists and open your playlist to watch its videos. New Playlist Name dialog with an example name and Create and Cancel buttons. Give the playlist a name, then select Create. This example uses “Watch this weekend”. Local playlists are stored by OpenTubeX. They are separate from public YouTube playlists, and adding a video does not download it. See Downloads to save media for offline use.

title: Open settings
description: Find videos, follow channels, and organize your local library.
text: Select your profile icon to open the quick settings menu. Choose All settings . Select a category or use settings search to find an option by name. OpenTubeX quick settings menu with the All settings gear in the upper-right corner. Select the gear at the top right of quick settings to open All settings. Start with Playback and settings for captions, autoplay, appearance, and SponsorBlock. Back up your library once you have it set up.

title: Organize channels with profiles
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Profiles group your subscribed channels into separate feeds, such as music, learning, or news. They are channel groups within the app, not separate Google accounts.

title: Create a profile
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage → Data . Select Manage Subscriptions to open the profile manager. Choose Create New Profile . Enter a name, choose its appearance, then select Create Profile . Profile Manager showing the color picker, a Learning profile name, profile preview, and Create Profile button. Choose a color and name, check the profile preview, then select Create Profile. The default All Channels profile collects your subscriptions. Use an additional profile when you want to focus on a subset.

title: Switch the feed you see
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Open the profile menu from the profile icon. Choose a profile in the profile selector. Open Subscriptions to view that profile’s channels. An empty profile has no channels to show. Switching profiles is not a way to create separate watch-history or playlist libraries.

title: Add channels
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: To add a new channel, switch to your desired profile, open the channel, and select Subscribe . The channel is also included in All Channels . To organize channels you already follow: Open Manage Subscriptions and choose the profile you want to edit. Select channels from the available channel list. Choose Add Selected To Profile . Return to your subscription feed and check the active profile.

title: Remove channels carefully
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Switch to a profile and use Unsubscribe on a channel to remove it from that group. The profile manager also offers bulk selection for managing channels. Removing a channel from All Channels removes it from the other profiles too. If you only want it out of one group, edit that group instead. Export your subscriptions before reorganizing a large library.

title: Back up profiles
description: Create focused subscription feeds and manage channels in bulk.
text: Use Settings → Data & Storage → Data → Export Subscriptions → Export OpenTubeX . That format preserves profile information for importing on another OpenTubeX installation. See Back up your library .

title: Importing and backing up data
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.

title: Find the import and export controls
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Open your profile menu and select All settings . Select Data & Storage . Open the Data tab. Use Import YouTube Takeout ZIP for a downloaded YouTube archive, or choose a separate import or export action for individual files. Data settings with a YouTube Takeout ZIP import button and separate import and export actions. Desktop Data settings. Import a YouTube Takeout ZIP directly, or use an action for an individual file.

title: Import subscriptions
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Export subscriptions from your previous app. For YouTube, request a YouTube data export through Google Takeout , including subscriptions. For a YouTube Takeout ZIP, select Import YouTube Takeout ZIP , then choose the categories to import. For other exports, select Import Subscriptions and choose the individual file. Wait for the import result. Open Subscriptions , check the active profile, and refresh the feed. Supported subscription formats include OpenTubeX / FreeTube .db , YouTube Takeout .csv , .json , or .opml , NewPipe .json , and LibreTube backup or FreeTube export .json . A JSON file must contain the expected export data; renaming a different file does not convert it.

title: Get your subscriptions from YouTube
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Follow the Google Takeout walkthrough to export subscriptions, history, and playlists. It covers export selection, the JSON history format, and importing the ZIP directly.

title: Move from another app
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Export a subscription file from your previous app, then transfer it to the device running OpenTubeX. Use a subscriptions export rather than a full archive when your app offers both. For OpenTubeX or FreeTube, keep the original .db file; for NewPipe, use its subscriptions .json export. Import the file with the steps above.

title: Import history or playlists
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: In the Data tab, choose Import History , Import Playlists , or Import search history . Select the matching exported file and wait for the result. Open the corresponding library page to check the imported entries. History accepts OpenTubeX / FreeTube .db, YouTube Takeout .json, and LibreTube backup .json. Search history accepts OpenTubeX / FreeTube .db and YouTube Takeout .json. Import Playlists accepts OpenTubeX / FreeTube .db exports and individual YouTube Takeout playlist .csv files. To import multiple Takeout playlists together, use Import YouTube Takeout ZIP .

title: Back up your library
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage → Data . Select Export Subscriptions , then Export OpenTubeX to keep OpenTubeX profiles and subscriptions. Export History , Playlists , search history , and Settings separately if you want to keep those too. Save the files in a backup location you can find on your other device. To restore, use the matching import actions on that device. Exports contain your personal viewing data. Store them privately. Settings exports omit device-specific and experimental options, such as proxy configuration, external-player paths, and screenshot folders. Downloaded video and audio files are separate from these exports; copy those files separately if you need them.

title: If an import fails
description: Bring subscriptions and history with you, and save a copy of your library.
text: Check the file type against the supported formats above and make sure you selected the correct action. For YouTube Takeout ZIPs, check that the archive contains the selected data and that history was exported as JSON. Keep the original export unchanged. If an import reports skipped items, inspect the result before assuming everything transferred. See Troubleshooting for the next steps.

title: Import from Google Takeout
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Google Takeout exports your Google account data. OpenTubeX can import subscriptions, watch history, search history, and playlists directly from the ZIP; you do not need to sign in to Google inside OpenTubeX.

title: Choose your YouTube data
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Open Google Takeout in English in your browser and sign in to the account you use for YouTube. Choose Deselect all , then select YouTube and YouTube Music . Open All YouTube data included . Deselect everything in that dialog, then select subscriptions , history , and/or playlists for the data you want. Confirm with OK . Selecting only these categories keeps the export smaller. If you use more than one Google account, check which account is selected before exporting. Google Takeout content-options dialog with history selected. Select history for watch and search history. You can also select subscriptions and playlists. The screenshots show the relevant controls, but are not captures of today’s interface. Google may change the layout and labels.

title: Choose JSON for history
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: In the YouTube and YouTube Music entry, open Multiple formats . Change History to JSON and confirm with OK . Select Next step . Google Takeout format dialog with history set to JSON. Set history to JSON before requesting the export. Google Takeout YouTube entry showing JSON format, one data type selected, and the Next step button. After making your choices, the buttons may read JSON format and a count of selected types rather than Multiple formats and All YouTube data included. This example includes history only. This step matters for watch and search history. OpenTubeX expects a JSON history export, not Takeout’s HTML version. Subscription exports use CSV. Renaming an HTML file to .json does not convert it.

title: Create and download the export
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Choose Send download link via email , Export once , and .zip . Select Create export . Wait for Google to prepare the archive. Use the download link when it is ready; Google may ask you to sign in again. Download the ZIP. If Google splits the export into several archives, import each ZIP that contains YouTube data. You do not need to upload the archive to another website. Creating an export does not delete your data from Google. Google’s export help covers delivery options and account-specific problems.

title: Import the ZIP
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: In OpenTubeX, open your profile menu, choose All settings , then Data & Storage → Data . Choose Import YouTube Takeout ZIP and select the downloaded ZIP. OpenTubeX detects subscriptions, watch history, search history, and playlists in the archive. Uncheck anything you do not want to import, then choose Import selected data . Check the corresponding library pages. Refresh the subscription feed to fetch channel uploads. Takeout ZIP import screen with checkboxes for detected subscriptions, watch history, playlists, and search history. You can still extract the ZIP and import individual files from Takeout/YouTube and YouTube Music/ : choose subscriptions/subscriptions.csv with Import Subscriptions , history/watch-history.json with Import History , history/search-history.json with Import search history , or a CSV in playlists/ with Import Playlists . OpenTubeX Data settings showing Import YouTube Takeout ZIP and separate data import actions. Choose Import YouTube Takeout ZIP to select the archive directly.

title: If something is missing
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Only HTML history files: create another export with History set to JSON. No supported YouTube data found: check the account and the selected data categories. The ZIP importer recognizes English Takeout folder and file names; if yours are translated, use Google Takeout in English for a new export or extract the archive and try the supported individual file imports. The archive’s archive_browser.html is an index, not importable data. Older history is missing: the export can only contain data Google still retains. Previously deleted activity may not be recoverable. A channel is missing after import: check the import result and your active profile . A removed channel or incomplete export may need investigation. A playlist video shows only its ID: Takeout’s playlist CSV includes video IDs and timestamps, but no video titles or durations. Keep your original archive until you have checked the imported data. See Importing and backing up data for other supported formats.

title: Sources and image credits
description: Import subscriptions, history, and playlists from a YouTube Takeout ZIP.
text: Takeout instructions are adapted from FreeTube’s subscription and history guides ( MIT license ), with OpenTubeX-specific import steps. General export behavior is checked against Google Account Help . The three Google Takeout UI screenshots are reproduced unchanged from positron48’s source images , published with Positroid’s September 2025 walkthrough . Google product visuals belong to Google and are shown for instructional purposes. See Google’s educational-use guidance . OpenTubeX is not affiliated with Google.

title: Playback and settings
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.

title: Use the player
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: Open a video. Move the pointer over the player, or tap it on a phone, to reveal controls. Use play/pause, the seek bar, and volume to control playback. Open the player’s settings menu to change quality or playback speed. Available qualities depend on the video and playback engine. Use the captions control to select a subtitle track when one is available. Use fullscreen for a larger view. On desktop, Picture-in-Picture keeps a floating player visible while you work elsewhere. Some controls move into the player’s overflow menu when space is limited. Live streams may not support seeking through the full video.

title: Set your playback defaults
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: Open Settings → Playback . Adjust default quality, playback rate, or autoplay options to suit your connection and viewing preferences. Set your preferred caption language and appearance if you use subtitles. Open another video to check your defaults. Playback settings showing subtitle, autoplay, volume, and Picture-in-Picture preferences. Desktop Playback settings. Player controls change the current video; settings let you choose defaults. Start Videos Automatically , Autoplay Recommended Videos , and Autoplay Playlist Videos control different behaviors. Turn off the ones you do not want. Per-channel settings can override global preferences, so check those if one channel behaves differently.

title: Find and customize keyboard shortcuts
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: On desktop, open Keyboard Shortcuts from the profile menu to see the current bindings. Select a shortcut and press a new combination to change it. This is also the place to check the bindings for play/pause, seeking, captions, fullscreen, and Picture-in-Picture. Shortcuts can be customized, so the displayed bindings are the source of truth. When typing in search or another text field, move focus back to the player before using playback keys.

title: Choose appearance and content settings
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: Appearance: choose a theme and adjust layout and thumbnails. Subscriptions: adjust feed refresh and display options. Add-ons: configure SponsorBlock and other optional services. Choose which SponsorBlock categories should be skipped automatically. Privacy: review viewing privacy options. Data & Storage: import or export your library and inspect storage usage. Sync: connect your devices for encrypted synchronization. Keep recovery information private and make a backup before changing your setup. See the SponsorBlock guide for skip behaviors and Privacy and watch history for recording controls. Use settings search when you know an option’s name but not its category. The Features page explains additional options such as transcripts and per-channel playback settings.

title: Android and Linux differences
description: Control playback, captions, autoplay, and the options you use most.
text: On Android, tap to show player controls. Background playback can continue when you switch apps; Android’s media notification provides playback controls. If it stops after the screen locks, see background playback troubleshooting . On Linux Wayland, the automatic Picture-in-Picture trigger for minimizing the window is unavailable. Use When the window loses focus or is switched away instead. Desktop window and external-player options do not all apply to Android.

title: Downloads and offline viewing
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.

title: Set up downloads
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open Settings → Downloads and turn on Enable Downloads if needed. Choose a Download Folder you can write to and that has enough free space. On desktop, allow time for any required managed tools to download. OpenTubeX uses yt-dlp and FFmpeg for download tasks; tool options depend on your platform. Downloads settings showing Enable Downloads, Download Folder, concurrent downloads, and bandwidth limit. Select the folder icon in Download Folder to choose where files are saved. Android uses its own storage picker and download implementation. Grant access to your chosen folder when prompted; desktop executable paths and the choice of system-installed tools do not apply there.

title: Download a video or audio
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open a video or its menu and select Download Video . In the download dialog, choose the offered format and quality, or an audio-only option when you want sound without video. Confirm the download. Open Downloads from the top bar or profile menu to see progress and queued items. Downloads need a working connection until they finish. Higher-quality video usually uses more storage. Subtitles can be downloaded when offered for the selected video.

title: Play a completed download
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open Downloads and find a completed item. Choose Play download to watch the saved media. On desktop, use Show in Folder to locate the file in your file manager. Keep the file in its saved location if you want OpenTubeX to find it again. Clearing an entry from the list and permanently deleting its file are different actions; read the confirmation before removing media.

title: Download a playlist
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open a playlist’s menu and choose Download Playlist when available. Review the download options before starting: a large playlist can use significant space. The Downloads panel shows the queued work.

title: Manage a failed download
description: Save video or audio, manage the queue, and find your downloaded files.
text: Open Downloads and read the item’s error. Check your connection, free space, and access to the download folder. On desktop, check managed tool updates under Settings → Advanced → External Software if the error mentions yt-dlp or FFmpeg. Use Retry download after fixing the cause. If the video itself will not play, start with playback troubleshooting . Include the download error and platform when reporting a bug .

title: SponsorBlock and other add-ons
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: SponsorBlock uses community-contributed segment timings to identify sponsors and other sections inside videos. Coverage depends on contributions: an unmarked segment cannot be skipped automatically.

title: Enable SponsorBlock
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: Open Settings → Add-ons . Find SponsorBlock and turn on Enable SponsorBlock . Review each category’s skip option rather than assuming they all behave the same. Open a video with known segments and check the seek bar. SponsorBlock enabled in Add-ons settings with separate Skip Option menus for Sponsor, Unpaid Self Promotion, and Interaction Reminder. Enable SponsorBlock, then choose each category’s Skip Option. Categories can use different behaviors.

title: Choose a skip behavior
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: Option What it does Auto Skip Skips segments in that category automatically. Prompt To Skip Offers a choice when a segment is reached. Show In Seek Bar Marks the segment without automatically skipping it. Do Nothing Disables the category’s skipping behavior. Choose different behaviors for categories such as sponsorships and intros. Show notice after a segment is skipped controls the notification; it does not enable or disable skipping itself.

title: If the wrong part is skipped
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: Check which category is responsible. Change that category to Prompt To Skip or Show In Seek Bar while investigating. Retry the affected section. If needed, temporarily disable SponsorBlock to compare playback. Segment timing comes from contributors and can be inaccurate. When reporting an OpenTubeX problem, include the public video URL, segment time, category, and chosen behavior.

title: Contributions and identity
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: Enable SponsorBlock Submission is separate from enabling playback skipping. Review it if you want to contribute. Keep the SponsorBlock Private User ID private; it is not something to include in a bug report. Leaving the custom ID empty allows the app to use its generated ID.

title: Other add-ons
description: Choose which segments to skip and configure optional metadata services.
text: In Settings → Add-ons , review Use DeArrow Video Titles , Use DeArrow for thumbnails , and Enable Return YouTube Dislike if you want alternative titles, thumbnails, or dislike information. These are optional services and their results may differ from YouTube’s own display. Enabling an add-on makes requests to its service. The privacy policy’s network exposure table describes what each service can observe. An add-on outage does not necessarily mean the video provider itself is unavailable.

title: Troubleshooting and bug reports
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.

title: A video will not play
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Try a second public video. If only one fails, it may be removed, private, region-restricted, or otherwise unavailable. Check your connection and restart OpenTubeX. Update the app . YouTube changes can break extraction in older versions. If you changed playback or provider settings, review them under Playback and Advanced . Try returning the affected option to its default and retry the same video. Check existing issues for the same error before opening a report. For buffering, try a lower quality in the player. If you use a proxy or an alternative provider, check whether the problem also happens without that configuration. Note which setting made a difference.

title: Imports or subscriptions look incomplete
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Check the active profile and try All Channels . Review feed filters and refresh the subscription feed. For an import, check the success or skipped-item message and confirm that you used a supported format . Keep the original export so you can retry or investigate missing entries. An imported channel list does not instantly contain every video. Refreshing the feed needs a working connection. Do not clear your data as a first troubleshooting step.

title: Downloads fail or saved files are missing
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Check the chosen download folder, storage permission, and free space. Moving or deleting a saved file outside OpenTubeX can make its list entry unavailable. On desktop, a download error mentioning external tools may require updating the managed tools. Follow the download troubleshooting steps .

title: Android background playback stops
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Confirm that playback works with the app in the foreground. Open Android’s app information for OpenTubeX and review its battery/background usage settings. Allow background activity if Android has restricted it; names vary by device. Check notification permission if media controls are missing. Test again with the screen locked and note whether the problem happens on Wi-Fi, mobile data, or both. Include your Android version and device model in a report. Desktop and Android behavior may differ.

title: The app will not open after installation
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Check that the package matches your processor and meets the requirements on the Downloads page . Extract portable archives before running them. On Linux, check the executable permission for an AppImage. On macOS, review the first-launch instructions in the installation guide . Before reinstalling or clearing storage, export your data if the app still opens. Clearing application data can remove your local library and settings.

title: Report a bug
description: Work through common problems and give maintainers the details they need.
text: Search the OpenTubeX issue tracker for your error or symptoms. If no existing issue matches, select New issue and use the bug-report template. Include the OpenTubeX version, operating system/version, installation method, and whether you use a regular release or nightly build. For Android, include the device model. Write numbered steps that reproduce the problem, what you expected, and what happened instead. Include the affected video URL if it is public and relevant. Copy the exact error text and attach a screenshot or short recording if it explains the problem. Mention any settings changes or workarounds you tested. Remove personal information from screenshots and logs. Do not attach cookies, passwords, sync recovery information, or your full viewing database to a public issue. For help using the app, you can also ask in the Matrix community or Fluxer community .

title: Choose a content provider
description: Understand Local API, Invidious, fallback, and video proxying.
text: A content provider retrieves video and channel information. It is separate from your local subscription library and from the player that plays the media.

title: Local API and Invidious
description: Understand Local API, Invidious, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Local API retrieves information directly from YouTube using the extractor included with OpenTubeX. YouTube receives those requests. If a YouTube change breaks extraction, an app update may be needed. Invidious API retrieves information through the Invidious server you select. That server contacts YouTube on your behalf and can observe your requests. Its availability depends on the operator and whether YouTube is blocking it. Neither option requires you to transfer your local subscriptions to a YouTube account. Choosing Invidious alone does not guarantee that every connection avoids YouTube: video proxying, fallback, and other enabled features also matter.

title: Change the provider
description: Understand Local API, Invidious, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Open Settings → Advanced . Find Preferred API Backend under the provider settings. Choose Local API or Invidious API . If choosing Invidious, review Current Invidious Instance and select the server you intend to use. Retry the same search or video to check the change. Advanced settings showing Preferred API Backend, fallback, stream extraction, and video proxy controls. Preferred API Backend and fallback are in the Video and metadata providers section of Advanced settings. Use settings search if the controls are not immediately visible. Choose an instance you trust rather than pasting an unknown server address solely because it appears in an error workaround.

title: Understand fallback
description: Understand Local API, Invidious, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Fallback allows the app to try another backend when the preferred backend fails. This can improve availability, but it can also send requests to a service you were trying to avoid. Search settings for fallback , review the setting, and disable it if you need to control which provider receives requests. Record your original settings before troubleshooting so you can restore them afterward.

title: Proxy video through Invidious
description: Understand Local API, Invidious, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Search settings for Proxy Videos Through Invidious to review video proxying. When supported by the selected playback path, this sends video requests through the instance rather than directly to YouTube. Proxying can affect speed and availability. Do not assume this switch controls external players or every playback engine. OpenTubeX’s privacy policy describes exposure for local extraction, Invidious, and yt-dlp separately.

title: When a provider stops working
description: Understand Local API, Invidious, fallback, and video proxying.
text: Try another public video, check for an app update, and check whether the selected instance is reachable. If you change providers as a test, note whether search, channel pages, or playback improved; that distinction helps a bug report .

title: Privacy and watch history
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: OpenTubeX keeps its library on your device by default. It reduces reliance on the YouTube website, but it does not make network requests anonymous. For details, see the privacy policy .

title: Choose what to remember
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Open Settings → Privacy . Review Remember Watch History and Remember Search History . Review Save Watched Progress if you want to resume videos where you left off. For viewing statistics, open Settings → General and review Enable Watch Statistics . Privacy settings showing watch history, search history, and Save Watched Progress controls. Use the history toggles to choose what to remember and Save Watched Progress to control resume behavior. Turning off future recording is different from deleting existing entries. Use the relevant removal action when you also want to clear saved data.

title: Limit history retention
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage → Storage and find Automatic History Retention (Days) in the watch-history controls. Leave it blank to keep history indefinitely, or enter a positive whole number to retain a limited number of days. Saving a retention period removes older entries immediately and continues applying the limit while the app is open. Export history first if you may want it later.

title: Clear data
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Search settings for Remove Watch History or Clear Search History and Cache , select the action you need, and read its confirmation. Clearing watch history is not the same as unsubscribing or removing playlists. For storage and cache cleanup, see Data and storage . Avoid clearing every category to troubleshoot a single playback problem.

title: Understand network privacy
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Local extraction and downloads can contact YouTube directly. Invidious sends relevant requests to the chosen instance; video proxying and fallback affect which other connections occur. SponsorBlock, DeArrow, and other add-ons contact their respective services when used. Sync sends the selected data to your configured server; review the sync mode and its encryption before relying on it. Internet connectivity checks sends small requests to a GrapheneOS-hosted service to check internet access. Review its toggle in Privacy settings. A receiving service can observe your IP address and request details unless the relevant connection is routed through an intermediary. Profiles are not separate security identities. See Choose a content provider for the provider settings, and the network exposure table for service-specific details.

title: Share a useful bug report privately
description: Choose what the app remembers and understand which services receive requests.
text: Before attaching a screenshot or log to a public issue, remove cookies, passwords, recovery information, and personal viewing data. Usually a public video URL, exact error, app version, and reproduction steps are more useful than an entire database.

title: Data and storage
description: Locate your desktop profile, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: Use data exports to transfer your library between devices. Use the storage view when you need to locate the desktop profile or understand disk usage.

title: Open the desktop profile directory
description: Locate your desktop profile, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage . Select Storage . Choose Open profile directory to open the current profile folder in your file manager. This is more reliable than assuming a fixed path: portable apps, sandboxed packages, and development builds can use different locations. Android uses its own application storage and does not offer the same desktop file-manager workflow.

title: Understand the files
description: Locate your desktop profile, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: File Contents profiles.db Profiles and subscriptions settings.db Application preferences playlists.db Local playlists and saved videos history.db Watch history and saved progress search-history.db Saved searches subscription-cache.db Cached subscription-feed entries These are application data files, not downloaded video files. Downloads are saved in your configured Download Folder . The profile folder may contain additional caches, session data, and files used by other features.

title: Back up or move to another device
description: Locate your desktop profile, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: For normal transfers, use the export and import actions . They let you choose what to transfer without copying device-specific settings indiscriminately. If you need a full desktop profile backup, close OpenTubeX before copying its profile directory to a private backup location. Copy downloaded media separately. Do not edit or replace live database files while the app is running.

title: Free storage
description: Locate your desktop profile, understand stored files, and clean up safely.
text: Open Settings → Data & Storage → Storage and review the categories and their descriptions. Prefer clearing a replaceable cache when you only want to reclaim cached data. Read the confirmation before clearing history or other library records. To remove downloaded media, use the Downloads panel and review whether the action clears its list entry or permanently deletes the file. Storage tab with a disk-usage chart and separate cards for downloaded media, download history records, and replaceable caches. The Storage tab separates downloaded media, records, and replaceable caches so you can choose what to clear. Cleared caches may need to be fetched again, which uses your connection. A cache is not a backup of your subscriptions, playlists, or history. See Privacy and watch history for retention and deletion controls.
